title: Durable Foundation prelaunch capture context
description: Objective: persist the immutable evidence needed to connect one prepared workspace to that same attempt's postlaunch capture without process-local mutable state. MEASURED at HEAD f81ab75: Foundation reservations store only request digest/attempt identities, Foundation context records store only inputManifestDigest for rendered context, and captureResult receives no sealed input, workspace assignment, trusted scope, or prelaunch observation. Deliverable: a focused daemon codec/identity/ledger for a versioned FoundationCaptureContext record committed before physical launch and read by derived captureRef. The record binds durable attempt/reservation identities, host catalog identity, exact worktree assignment, full sealed input manifest, authoritative declared scopes, clean prelaunch ScopeObservation, bounded baseline digest, and the closed M1 artifact declaration NONE. NOT in scope: resolving the catalog, creating/scanning a worktree, changing service launch order, invoking captureResult, provider launch, or result sealing. Owned paths: apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-capture-context-contract.ts/.js, foundation-capture-context-ledger.ts/.js, foundation-capture-context-ledger.test.ts. Consumer: the prepare-before-launch lifecycle task created by this split; record its exact id before completion. Verification command: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck; $a=$LASTEXITCODE; pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test; $b=$LASTEXITCODE; Write-Host "DAEMON_TC=$a DAEMON_TEST=$b"; if ($a -ne 0 -or $b -ne 0) { exit 1 }`, with nonzero printed counts.
definitionOfDone: The exact versioned record binds projectId, sessionId, nodeKey, attempt aggregate/id, reservation/request digest, catalog digest plus repository/scope/base identities, exact worktree assignment identity/real root, authoritative declared paths, full sealed WorkspaceInputManifest, clean prelaunch ScopeObservation, scanner baseline digest, artifact declaration NONE, observedAt, and a record digest covering every field.

Codec admission snapshots own data descriptors once, enforces exact keys plus existing workspace/scope bounds and seals, deep-freezes the result, and refuses malformed/accessor/extra/missing/over-limit/unsealed/cross-field-mismatched input with exact FOUNDATION_CAPTURE_CONTEXT_* code at DAEMON_FOUNDATION_CAPTURE.

Aggregate, command, correlation, event, request, and captureRef identities are domain-separated and derived only from the bound durable identities/digests; identical preparation replays byte-identically, while any changed field under the same attempt refuses as a conflict and preserves the first bytes.

The real SqliteEventStore ledger commit/read path verifies event type, aggregate/project/version, payload digest, record digest, and captureRef binding; absent, ambiguous, truncated, reordered, forged, or unreadable history remains UNKNOWN under distinct stable code/layer and never returns a partial context.

Focused tests assert a real-store accepted commit/reopen/read control, exact code plus layer for a nonzero generated field-sweep and hostile history roster, raw event/decision counts on replay/conflict, and no module-global map; mutations dropping one digest field or adopting the last conflicting record redden named tests.

The exact production consumer task id is recorded, daemon typecheck/test exit 0 with nonzero Test Files/Tests counts, both LF bridges plain-Node load, and each production source targets <=250 lines and stays below 400.
taskRails: This ledger stores facts already produced by other authorities; it must not resolve a repository, invent a scope, scan bytes, create a worktree, or decide launch/result truth.
No singleton variable or process-local map may carry context between prepare and capture; only the immutable derived captureRef and durable record may do so.
Conflicting or unreadable history fails closed and preserves first durable bytes; never pick first/last opportunistically or restamp an upstream runner refusal.
Artifact declaration is the closed M1 literal NONE; no caller-supplied artifact list enters this record.

MEASURED CONSTRAINT WORTH THE ARCHITECT'S ATTENTION. canonicalDigest is NOT re-exported from @moe/runner's barrel (checked at HEAD: git show HEAD:packages/runner/src/index.ts has no canonical.js re-export). There is no tsconfig paths mapping and a deep relative import fails TS6059, so the codec CANNOT recompute a producer's seal without reimplementing the hash formula, which the epic rails forbid. So "seals" in DoD 2 is implemented as: every digest-shaped field must BE a digest (64-hex, code FOUNDATION_CAPTURE_CONTEXT_UNSEALED), and the independently produced halves must AGREE (code FOUNDATION_CAPTURE_CONTEXT_FIELD_MISMATCH, five rules: baselineDigest vs inputManifest.sha256, observation.baseIdentity vs inputManifest.baseIdentity, assignment.realWorktreePath vs observation.worktreeIdentity, projectId vs both catalogAuthority.projectId and assignment.projectId, attemptId vs assignment.attemptId). The module comment states plainly that it never claims to have recomputed a seal.

THE IDENTITY BLOCK LIVES HERE, taking the safety valve step-2 disclosed. Seven namespaces, all new, none reusing the golden-pinned moe-foundation-context/1: family: -ref/1:, /1: (aggregate), -command/1:, -correlation/1:, -event/1:, -principal/1:, -request/1:.

THE CARRIED VALUE IS ONE STRING, WHICH IS THE POINT OF TASK RAIL 2. captureRef derives from the SLOT alone (version, projectId, sessionId, attemptAggregateId, attemptId, nodeKey); the aggregate derives FROM THE CAPTUREREF, not from the slot. So the capture side needs to carry nothing but the ref: it re-derives the aggregate from it, reads, and re-derives the ref from the record's own fields to confirm it got the record it asked for. Deriving the aggregate from the slot instead would have forced the capture side to carry the slot too, and a second carried value is a second thing that can disagree.

THE CONFLICT PROTOCOL IS AN ASYMMETRY, AND BOTH ARMS ARE TESTED. recordDigest is IN the request preimage and OUT of the command preimage. A changed CONTENT field therefore reuses the command id under a different request -> store throws IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT -> FOUNDATION_CAPTURE_CONTEXT_LEDGER_REPLAY_DIVERGED. A changed reservationDigest is a different command against an aggregate already at version 1 -> store RETURNS a no-business-effect decision -> FOUNDATION_CAPTURE_CONTEXT_LEDGER_EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT. Both arms assert the first bytes still read back and that the aggregate still holds exactly ONE event, because a second call that does not throw is also what a double write looks like.

READER VERIFIES ALL FIVE THINGS DoD 4 NAMES, each with its own code: event type (EVENT_TYPE_UNEXPECTED), aggregate + sequence + domain schema version (BINDING_MISMATCH), payload byte identity via the codec's decode -> re-encode -> sameBytes (UNREADABLE, carrying the codec's verbatim code in codecCode), record digest (same path), and captureRef binding by re-deriving from the decoded record (REF_MISMATCH). Absent is its own code; duplicates are COUNTED and refused, never picked. A throwing store answers UNREADABLE, never ABSENT — "no record" and "cannot read" lead an operator to opposite actions.

The plan's drill (iii) — reader skips the re-encode/sameBytes — was run at step-1 against the codec that owns that step, and went red there.

THE MOST IMPORTANT THING IN THIS STEP IS A DEFECT I FOUND IN MY OWN WORK. I drilled the writer to ECHO the caller's candidate on a REPLAYED disposition instead of reading the durable event. It SURVIVED GREEN, and the equivalence argument for why looked airtight: the store answers REPLAYED only on a matching request identity, the request preimage contains recordDigest, and recordDigest covers all fifteen bound fields — so on any genuine replay the candidate necessarily encodes to the same bytes as the durable record, and every byte comparison in the suite passes either way. I nearly filed it as an honest equivalent mutant. It is not one. Reading the durable event RE-RUNS the codec's byte verification; echoing the caller returns clean bytes for a store whose record was edited underneath. So I added the one test that separates them: commit through a REAL store so the REPLAYED disposition is genuine, then serve readEvents from a poisoned view whose payload has one hex character flipped inside a bound digest value. The real writer refuses FOUNDATION_CAPTURE_CONTEXT_READER_UNREADABLE; the echoing mutant returns ok. Re-drilled: RED.
Earlier in the task the same method caught two more of my own errors — a "no module-global map" test that survived a real module-level cache because the commit path never warms one (fixed by making the warm read come first), and a drill that read a cache it never populated.

ADVERSARIAL CASES the step named: a record sitting EXACTLY on every published limit is ADMITTED and one entry past it refuses — the pair is what proves the comparison is > and not >=, since an off-by-one guard passes every refusal case on its own; a 4096-entry sealed manifest answers LIMIT_EXCEEDED rather than MALFORMED, which is the whole reason the pre-snapshot descriptor length read exists; an accessor smuggled three levels down into an observed entry is caught by snapshot-once; and two attempts sealed and re-sealed INTERLEAVED (A, B, A, B) hold isolation, with both dispositions, both byte sets, both refs and both row counts asserted — a write-read-write-read order would not have noticed a shared command id.
